steps.a: And then Mia woke up, and it was all a dream.
steps.b: Mia hung the cracked medal on her wall. She hadn't won, but she had finished the race, and next year she knew she could.
steps.reveal: The first ending throws the story away. The second one settles the problem and shows how Mia has changed. That's a resolution.

cards.title: The climax
cards.body: The climax is the top of the mountain: the moment of greatest tension, where the character faces the problem head-on. It usually comes about two-thirds to three-quarters of the way through the story.

cards.title: The character acts
cards.body: In a strong climax, the character makes something happen: a choice, a brave move, a clever idea. Avoid endings where luck or someone else solves everything.

cards.title: The resolution
cards.body: After the climax, slow down. Show what happens next and how things have changed: what did the character learn, win, lose or decide? Leave the reader satisfied, not confused.

cards.title: Find the change
cards.prompt: Tap the two words that show how Ravi has changed at the end.
cards.text: Ravi used to hide at the back of the class. Now he raised his hand first, and he smiled when everyone turned to listen.

prompts: How does your character make the climax happen?
What has changed for your character by the end?
